messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated streaming tail latency in eu-west-1, error spike for push responses. Paging maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): on it. seeing alerts. paging dave + ryan.

dave (eng-sre): confirmed - streaming push frames/sec spiked ~3x at 10:12 UTC, 99th pct latency ~2.6s. HTTP poll endpoints OK.

ryan (eng-runtime): probable KV cache pressure + request fanout during large prompt windows. streaming codepath holding more connections -> memory churn.

maria (oncall): threshold: reduce streaming pressure while preserving user experience. proposals?

dave (eng-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) feature-flag to disable streaming in eu-west-1 (graceful fallback to final response/polling) 2) apply per-key streaming rate-limit (eg 150 rps) 3) temporarily reduce max concurrent streaming per-worker.

ryan (eng-runtime): agreed. do (1) then (2). implement flag so clients get normal non-streaming responses (no partial frames).

anna (customer-success): heads-up: top 3 customers on eu-west-1 reported timeouts in streaming SDKs. we're drafting a short advisory once we have the mitigation.

maria (oncall): dave, can you toggle the flag? i'll coord comms and pager handoff after change.

dave (eng-sre): doing the flag flip now. running command:
```
prodctl feature-flag set streaming_push eu-west-1 false --who=dave
```

sre-bot: feature-flag change queued: streaming_push.eu-west-1 -> false by dave at 10:18 UTC.

dave (eng-sre): change applied, propagation to edge ~30s. monitoring.

[~45s later]
dave (eng-sre): propagation confirmed. edge logs show STREAM_FRAME emits dropped, clients falling back to single final response. error rate down 60% in region. queue depth decreasing.

maria (oncall): nice. now apply soft rate limit to streaming fallback so new long-lived clients don't burst:
```
prodctl rate-limit set streaming_global eu-west-1 150rps --duration=30m
```

incident-bot: rate-limit policy applied: streaming_global.eu-west-1 = 150rps for 30m.

anna (customer-success): sending advisory to customers now. template: 
"We are temporarily disabling streaming responses in eu-west-1 to stabilize latency. You will receive final responses instead of incremental frames. We expect restoration within ~30-60 minutes. Contact us if you need priority handling."

maria (oncall): good template. @anna send to top customers and copy sales for any escalations.

dave (eng-sre): adding a short-term quota bump option for dedicated customers if CS asks, but prefer to keep quotas until we validate stabilization.

ryan (eng-runtime): monitoring metrics: token throughput up ~10% but CPU per-pod down, tail latency back under SLO for non-streaming clients. Keep flag set for 30 minutes then reassess.

maria (oncall): handoff in 20m to ryan. I'll update incident channel with follow-up and prepare a post-incident action list: root-cause triage, better streaming backpressure, client-side SDK fallback guidance.

anna (customer-success): PS: a customer asked for a one-line status blurb for their users: "We temporarily switched to single-response mode due to instability; streaming will return shortly." will send.

maria (oncall): thanks. marking this thread as mitigation in progress. will escalate to postmortem if flag required beyond 1h.

ryan (eng-runtime): noted for oncall. after handoff i'll watch for reenable window and coordinate canary re-enable with gradual fan-in.

maria (oncall): closing active paging to oncall. if new alerts fire, page the rotation. otherwise we'll log mitigation end and run RCA tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
